context.canonical_title: Linux 线上排查常用命令有哪些？

required_checks: Verify the answer covers both restored source rows asking for common Linux commands while honoring the canonical's online-troubleshooting scope rather than drifting into a generic system-design template.

Verify load average is not equated to CPU utilization and that runnable/uninterruptible-task interpretation is bounded to Linux semantics and cross-checked with CPU, blocked-task and pressure evidence.
Verify iostat sampling semantics are correct: the first report normally covers time since boot, later reports cover the sampling interval, and -y omits the first report.
Verify iostat %util is not treated as a universal saturation limit for parallel devices such as RAID and modern SSDs.
Verify PSI and cgroup-v2 memory.current, memory.events and memory.pressure are used as scoped pressure/accounting evidence rather than inferred from host totals alone.
Verify sar is presented as a historical activity source only when collection data exists, not as guaranteed retrospective data on every host.
Verify strace/perf are scoped deep-diagnosis tools with explicit production overhead and sensitive-output boundaries rather than default global probes.
Verify the concept-answer contract remains orally usable, gives selection/next-step conditions and contains at least three topic-specific answered follow-ups without fabricated incident metrics.
review_contract.promotion_boundary: Do not promote or fabricate human approval. This canonical remains in the pilot review scope and requires the repository's mandatory human-review attestation after evidence and deterministic audit pass.

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: The /proc Filesystem — Linux Kernel documentation
claims_to_check: /proc/loadavg exposes load averages and runnable-task information
/proc and related procfs entries expose process and system state used by monitoring tools

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: proc_loadavg(5) — Linux man-pages
claims_to_check: Linux load average includes tasks that are runnable or in uninterruptible state and therefore is not CPU utilization

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: PSI - Pressure Stall Information — Linux Kernel documentation
claims_to_check: CPU, memory and I/O pressure are exported through /proc/pressure
PSI quantifies time impact from resource contention rather than merely reporting capacity totals

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Control Group v2 — Linux Kernel documentation
claims_to_check: memory.current reports cgroup memory use, memory.events reports memory-limit/pressure events, and memory.pressure exposes scoped PSI

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: iostat manual — sysstat upstream
claims_to_check: the first report normally covers time since boot and subsequent reports cover time since the previous report; -y omits the first report
%util near 100% indicates saturation for serial request-serving devices but does not reflect performance limits for parallel devices such as RAID and modern SSDs

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: sar manual — sysstat upstream
claims_to_check: sar can collect, save and later report system activity data when collection has been configured

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: strace project documentation
claims_to_check: strace traces interactions including system calls and signals and can be filtered/scoped for diagnosis
